Pathology Findings:
Clinical Information: 58-year-old female with a non-painful, pigmented lesion on the left cheek. The lesion has been present for approximately one year, with a recent slight increase in size. Clinical concern for atypical nevus vs. seborrheic keratosis.
Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled with the patient's name and "left cheek," is a single shave biopsy of skin measuring 0.5 x 0.4 x 0.2 cm. The specimen is a tan-brown, slightly verrucous papule. The deep margin is inked black. The specimen is bisected and submitted entirely in one cassette.
Microscopic Description: Microscopic examination reveals an exophytic proliferation of benign basaloid keratinocytes. The architecture shows prominent acanthosis, papillomatosis, and the formation of numerous keratin-filled invaginations and horn pseudocysts. The basaloid cells are uniform in appearance with small, regular nuclei and no significant mitotic activity or pleomorphism. Within the underlying dermis, there is a mild, patchy, perivascular infiltrate composed of lymphocytes and occasional eosinophils. The deep and peripheral margins are free of the lesion. No evidence of dysplasia or malignancy is identified.
Diagnosis: Skin, left cheek, shave biopsy: Seborrheic keratosis, irritated.
Comment: The histologic features are characteristic of an irritated seborrheic keratosis. The irritation corresponds to the mild dermal inflammation seen microscopically. Clinical correlation is recommended.
Specimen: One piece of skin from the left cheek, measuring 0.5 x 0.4 x 0.2 cm.
Pathologist: Dr. James Peterson

Polysomnography Report
Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.
This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomnogram. Total sleep time was 345 minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%. Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, comprising only 10% of total sleep time.
Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. These events were predominantly obstructive apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%. The patient's baseline oxygen saturation was 95%. No significant periodic limb movements were noted.
Impression: The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to determine the optimal pressure for treatment.
Date of Interpretation: 06/20/2025

She was counseled that it is not contagious and typically resolves spontaneously in 6-8 weeks. CD20: Negative 
CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population. 
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.
